title: Analytics Dashboard
prompt: Design a customizable analytics dashboard with 12 charts, date filters and auto-refresh. Metric computation is server-owned. Widgets have different latency and freshness requirements; one failing chart must not block the others. Draw the component/data-flow architecture, define state owners and contracts, and explain performance, accessibility and recovery. No UI coding is required.
functionalReqs: Apply shared URL date/filter state to independent widgets
Load widgets progressively with local error/retry boundaries
Refresh visible widgets with bounded concurrency and consistent comparison windows
nonFunctionalReqs: 12 widgets, each at most 1,000 displayed points; 4 concurrent queries; hidden-tab refresh suspended.
Each chart has a title, units, textual summary and accessible table/download alternative; keyboard controls for filters and layout, distinguish data series beyond color.
Reject obsolete keys, show per-widget error and retain clearly marked stale data only when its range is visible. Never label old-range data as current.

scale.notes: 12 widgets, each at most 1,000 displayed points; 4 concurrent queries; hidden-tab refresh suspended.
scale.storage: 12 widgets × 1,000 points; concurrency 4; illustrative interview assumptions, not measured guarantees.

outOfScope: Backend sharding, ranking algorithms and infrastructure provisioning
Implementing a production UI inside this exercise
deepDives: Coordinate filter changes with a generation key but give each widget an independent query/error boundary. Limit parallel requests, pause refresh in hidden tabs and request server aggregation/downsampling for the visible chart resolution.
One slow widget returns a previous date range after filters change
A batched endpoint reduces requests but can couple slow widgets. Independent queries improve isolation; server snapshot tokens are needed if exact cross-widget consistency matters.
